clue.text: Compared with foreign currency, it's immaterial

blocks.note: beside can mean in comparison with, as in 'pale beside her sister'
the German mark, a foreign currency in 1997

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off how a sum looks when set against a foreign currency's value.
explanation.walkthrough: The Deutschmark was still Germany's currency when this appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: A point that is off target or irrelevant to the question in hand is said to be wide of, or beside, the mark.

clue.text: Winds may veer

blocks.note: surface reading: a weather forecast that the wind direction will shift
setter's reading: winds swing between warm and chilly gusts, like a person who keeps changing their mind

explanation.walkthrough: Taken literally, winds do this; the phrase is the idiom for wavering.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone alternately enthusiastic and indifferent, vacillating as changeable winds do.

clue.text: Partners concealing anger and alarm

indicators.note: concealing means the partners wrap round and hide the word for anger

blocks.note: South and North, partners at bridge
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A couple hide their anger and their alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge North plays with South, so 'partners' gives N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a warning device sounding a loud wail, so it is an alarm.

clue.text: Derelict building levelled with Cockney's grant

blocks.note: a building that has been levelled is down
handout, a grant, with the H dropped as a Cockney speaker would

explanation.surface: An abandoned building is demolished with the help of a grant from an East Ender.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, Londoners from the East End, are said to drop their aitches.
explanation.definitionFit: A derelict is a destitute vagrant, and a destitute homeless person is called this.

clue.text: Fail to use up your grass

indicators.note: up in a down entry means the word is written bottom to top

blocks.note: to omit something is to leave it out, failing to use it
thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: A warning that if you don't use your grass it will be wasted.
explanation.definitionFit: Timothy is a meadow grass grown widely for hay and pasture, so it is a type of grass.

clue.text: Note, new and old coin in change to count?

blocks.note: E is a musical note
N is short for new
a noble was a medieval English gold coin

explanation.surface: Someone counts their change: a banknote, a new coin and an old one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' and 'count' suggest money; the question mark flags the count as a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble someone is to raise them to the nobility, and making someone a count is one example.

clue.text: Amount of territory captured by Crusaders

blocks.note: first meaning: a measure of land area
second meaning: the port city in present-day Israel taken in 1104 and 1191

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase about conquered land; the second half is a place the Crusaders took.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land area of 4,840 square yards, and Acre is the coastal city the Crusaders seized twice.

clue.text: Criminal found in Leatherhead

blocks.note: kid is soft leather made from young goatskin
napper is old slang for the head

explanation.surface: A wanted criminal turns up in Leatherhead, a Surrey town.
explanation.walkthrough: Leatherhead is a town in Surrey, but it splits into two words here.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abducts a person and holds them for ransom is committing a serious crime.

clue.text: One can afford alternative imports from France

definitions.text: One can afford alternative imports from France

blocks.clueFragment: One can afford alternative imports from France
blocks.note: surface reading: a shopper who has the money for other goods shipped in from France

blocks.clueFragment: One can afford alternative imports from France
blocks.note: setter's reading: a phrase borrowed from French that affords, or offers, a second meaning

explanation.walkthrough: 'Afford' means provide, not pay for, and 'imports' means meanings, as in the import of a remark.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived term names a phrase with two readings, one usually risqué, so it gives alternative meanings.

clue.text: A worm one's chopped into four, perhaps

definitions.note: a four is a rowing crew; the answer is its members

indicators.note: a worm chopped into bits is in pieces that can be put back in any order

blocks.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A gardener's spade cuts a worm into four wriggling pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Four' is a rowing boat with four oars, not the number of pieces; the four rowers here are women.
explanation.definitionFit: A four in rowing is a boat crewed by four rowers, so female crew members are an example of a four.

clue.text: Receiver at first rather aggressive, driving into opponent

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of each word in the run that follows

blocks.note: first letter
first letter
first letter
first letter
first letter

explanation.surface: A football receiver gets hit hard by a defender charging into him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' covers all five following words, not only 'rather'.
explanation.definitionFit: A wireless set picks up broadcast signals, so it is a kind of receiver.

clue.text: Henry and one of his wives rejected cosmetic

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the wife's name is read from its end

blocks.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
Anne Boleyn or Anne of Cleves, wives of Henry VIII

explanation.surface: Henry VIII and a cast-off wife are linked with a beauty product.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry gives only H, yet the surface keeps him as Henry VIII so his wives make sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a reddish plant dye used on hair and skin, a traditional cosmetic preparation.

clue.text: Train set

blocks.note: first meaning: a London Underground train
second meaning: a television set, informally

explanation.walkthrough: 'Train set' looks like a toy railway; split it into two separate nouns. The Tube is London's Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: Londoners call the Underground railway and its trains the Tube, and a television receiver is colloquially the tube after its cathode-ray picture tube.

clue.text: Piece of verse from William Blake

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken straight out of the run of words that follows

blocks.note: inside williAM Blake, spanning the two names

explanation.surface: A quotation is taken from a poem by William Blake.
explanation.definitionFit: An iamb is a metrical foot, an unstressed syllable then a stressed one, so a small unit of poetry.

clue.text: On the other side after outward Channel crossing

indicators.note: outward keeps only the outside letters of the word that follows
after puts the other-side phrase behind the channel letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters
overleaf means on the other side of the page

explanation.surface: Something happens on the far shore after the outbound ferry trip across the Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel crossing' looks like one phrase, but the Channel only gives letters and 'crossing' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloverleaf is a motorway interchange whose looping slip roads look like a four-leaf clover, so it is a road crossing.

clue.text: With disturbance due, stay twenty-four hours

indicators.note: a disturbance throws things into disorder, so the following letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Because trouble is expected, someone is told to stay a full day.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuesday is one particular day of the week, and a day lasts twenty-four hours, so it is an example.

clue.text: Bring about one scamp's reformation

indicators.note: a reformation forms something again in a new shape, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to reform a young rascal.
explanation.definitionFit: In an older sense, to encompass a goal is to achieve or contrive it, which is to bring it about.

clue.text: Cut out and cut in quarters

indicators.note: in places the cutting word inside the compass bearing

blocks.note: to clip is to cut
east-south-east, a point lying between compass quarters, split as E and SE

explanation.surface: An instruction to cut something out and then chop it into four.
explanation.walkthrough: Quarters are compass directions here, not fractions: the bearing ESE opens to go round the cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse a rival is to outshine and supplant them, which is what cutting someone out means.

clue.text: Reduce music in part of service

indicators.note: to reduce something is to make it shorter, so the end of the musical word is dropped

blocks.note: a nocturne is a dreamy piece of night music

explanation.surface: A choirmaster wants less music during part of the church service.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the final E of NOCTURNE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturn is one of the divisions of Matins, the night office of psalms and readings in the Roman Catholic liturgy.

clue.text: Grandma eager to make up material

blocks.note: nan is a familiar name for a grandmother
keen means eager

explanation.surface: Grandmother is eager to sew up some cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth originally from Nanjing, so it is a fabric or material.

clue.text: Engagement ring lost -- in a stew

indicators.note: lost says a ring-shaped letter goes missing from the battle's name

blocks.note: the naval battle of Navarino, 1827
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Someone who has lost an engagement ring is in a stew about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engagement' is a battle, not a betrothal; take the O off NAVARINO, the 1827 sea battle off Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Navarin is a French mutton or lamb casserole with root vegetables, so it is a kind of stew.

clue.text: Very low-tech tool repairs hot line

indicators.note: repairs suggests the line is taken apart and put back together differently

blocks.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A low-tech engineer mends a telephone hotline.
explanation.definitionFit: A neolith is a polished stone implement from the New Stone Age, about as primitive as technology gets.

clue.text: Curry that contains honey

blocks.note: first meaning: to groom a horse with a currycomb
second meaning: the wax cells a bee fills

explanation.walkthrough: Curry here is not the dish but the verb for grooming a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Grooming a horse's coat with a currycomb is combing it, and the honeycomb in a hive is the comb that holds honey.

clue.text: Open event preceded by one in France

indicators.note: preceded by puts the French word for one in front of the event

blocks.note: un is French for one
a do is a party or social event

explanation.surface: An open sporting event in France is headed by a single competitor.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a parcel, button or lock is to open it, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Money in sport? Very little of it, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the coin's letter is written as it is spoken

blocks.note: RU is Rugby Union
p, a penny, is very little money; spelt out as the letter's name

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether sport pays, and hears that it pays very little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very little of it' means very little money: a single p or penny.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is the currency unit of India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka, so it is money.

clue.text: Nut about to be put in prison

indicators.note: put in places the short word for about inside the prison

blocks.note: pen, short for penitentiary
ca is circa, about

explanation.surface: A madman is about to be sent to prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nut' reads as a crazy person; it is the edible kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The pecan is the edible nut of a hickory tree from the southern United States.

clue.text: I heard you indulge in needlework

indicators.note: heard says the following words are to be spoken, not spelt

blocks.note: knitting is a form of needlework

explanation.surface: Someone says they hear their friend enjoys sewing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker but is the Roman numeral one.
explanation.definitionFit: I is the Roman numeral for one, and a unit is the number one or a single whole.

clue.text: What pupils do to master

blocks.note: first meaning: what students are at school to do
second meaning: to acquire a skill fully

explanation.walkthrough: 'Master' looks like the schoolmaster pupils answer to, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Schoolchildren acquire knowledge in class, and acquiring a skill thoroughly is mastering it, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Demonstrated - even if the lower classes withdrew

indicators.note: if the classes withdrew the word would still mean the same, so they sit inside it

blocks.note: the clue's opening word read a second time: evinced also means demonstrated
D and E are the lowest social grades in British market research

explanation.surface: A protest went ahead even though the working-class marchers pulled out.
explanation.walkthrough: Take DE out of the answer and EVINCED is left, which also means demonstrated: the clue says the meaning survives their withdrawal.
explanation.definitionFit: To evidence something is to show or prove it, so evidenced and demonstrated are synonyms in the past tense.

clue.text: Don't get committed - delay dealing with criminal

blocks.note: to sit on a matter is to put off dealing with it
a fence is a criminal who receives stolen goods

explanation.surface: Advice to stall before handling a criminal so as not to be sent to prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Committed' suggests being sent for trial; here it means taking a side.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying neutral and refusing to back either side of an argument is the idiom for not taking a position.
